next_review_trigger: Finance Act amendment or TRA update to professional VAT list

question_sw: Daktari anasema: 'Huduma za afya zimesamehewa VAT — kwa hivyo sijasajilishwa.' Je, hoja hii ni sahihi?
answer_sw: Hoja hii ina nuance muhimu. Kweli fulani: huduma za afya za msingi (basic health services) zinaweza kuwa exempt au zero-rated kwa VAT. Lakini: hii haimaanishi daktari hauhitaji KUSAJILIWA VAT. Hata kama huduma zako ziko exempt, unastahili kusajiliwa kama fani iliyodhibitiwa. Pia, si huduma zote za madaktari ni exempt — huduma za kibinafsi za hali ya juu, huduma za urembo, na zingine zinaweza kuwa taxable.
question_en: A doctor says: 'Health services are VAT-exempt — so I have not registered.' Is this argument correct?
answer_en: This argument has an important nuance. Partly true: basic health services may be exempt or zero-rated for VAT. But: this does not mean a doctor does not need to BE REGISTERED for VAT. Even if your services are exempt, you are still required to register as a regulated profession. Also, not all doctors' services are exempt — high-end private services, cosmetic services, and others may be taxable.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Ninaendesha biashara ya ushauri wa IT (IT consulting) — si fani iliyodhibitiwa. Je, lazima nisajili VAT?
answer_sw: Kwa IT consultant asiye na leseni ya fani iliyodhibitiwa, kizingiti cha kawaida cha TZS 200M kwa miezi 12 kinatumika. Huhitajiki kusajili VAT mpaka mauzo yako yafike kizingiti hiki. Hata hivyo: kama una leseni ya uhandisi wa programu (software engineering) kutoka ERB au leseni nyingine ya kitaalamu, kanuni ya fani zinazodhibitiwa inaweza kutumika. Thibitisha hali yako maalum na TRA.
question_en: I run an IT consulting business — it is not a regulated profession. Must I register for VAT?
answer_en: For an IT consultant without a regulated professional licence, the standard threshold of TZS 200M per 12 months applies. You are not required to register for VAT until your sales reach this threshold. However: if you hold a software engineering licence from ERB or another professional licence, the regulated profession rule may apply. Confirm your specific situation with TRA.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Wakili mpya aliyeidhinishwa leo — anaweza kuanza kufanya kazi bila kusajili VAT kwanza?
answer_sw: Hapana — wakili aliyeidhinishwa hivi karibuni anapaswa kusajili VAT kama sehemu ya mahitaji ya kuweza kufanya mazoezi ya kisheria Tanzania. Ni vizuri kusajili VAT KABLA au WAKATI wa kuanza mazoezi — si baadaye. Kusimamia wateja bila usajili wa VAT unapoishia linapaswa kulipa inaweza kusababisha adhabu za kodi na matatizo na Tanganyika Law Society.
question_en: A newly admitted advocate today — can they start practising without first registering for VAT?
answer_en: No — a newly admitted advocate should register for VAT as part of the requirements to practise law in Tanzania. It is advisable to register for VAT BEFORE or AT THE TIME of starting practice — not later. Managing clients without VAT registration when you should be registered may result in tax penalties and complications with the Tanganyika Law Society.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Mhandisi ana ofisi ya kibinafsi na pia ana kazi ya mshahara serikalini. Je, anahitaji kusajili VAT kwa ofisi yake binafsi?
answer_sw: Ndiyo — hata kama mhandisi ana kazi ya mshahara serikalini, ofisi yake ya kibinafsi (consultancy) inastahili usajili wa VAT kwa sababu ana leseni ya kitaalamu ya ERB. Shughuli mbili tofauti: kazi ya mshahara (kodi inazingatiwa na mwajiri) na ofisi binafsi (lazima asimamie mwenyewe kodi ikiwa ni pamoja na VAT). Mapato yote ya ofisi binafsi lazima yaorodheshwe kwa TRA.
question_en: An engineer has a private office and also salaried government employment. Do they need to register for VAT for their private office?
answer_en: Yes — even if an engineer is salaried in government, their private office (consultancy) requires VAT registration because they hold an ERB professional licence. Two separate activities: salaried employment (tax managed by employer) and private office (must manage own taxes including VAT). All private office income must be declared to TRA.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: CPA aliyestaafu kazi bado ana leseni yake ya NBAA. Anahitaji kudumisha usajili wa VAT?
answer_sw: Kama CPA aliyestaafu bado ana leseni hai ya NBAA na bado anafanya kazi yoyote ya uhasibu au ukaguzi — hata kwa wateja wachache — usajili wa VAT bado unatumika. Kama amestaafu kabisa na HAJAFANYI biashara yoyote ya kitaalamu, anaweza kuomba TRA kufuta usajili wake wa VAT kwa mujibu wa taratibu sahihi. Hata hivyo, kuwa na leseni inayoendelea bila kufanya kazi mara nyingi si tatizo la VAT — tatizo linatokea ukifanya kazi bila usajili.
question_en: A retired CPA still holds their active NBAA licence. Do they need to maintain VAT registration?
answer_en: If a retired CPA still holds an active NBAA licence and is still doing any accounting or auditing work — even for a few clients — VAT registration still applies. If fully retired and NOT conducting any professional business, they may apply to TRA to deregister their VAT following proper procedures. However, holding a continuing licence while not working is generally not a VAT problem — the problem arises if working without registration.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Biashara yangu ya kawaida (duka la nguo) haijafika TZS 200M. Lakini pia mimi ni CPA. Je, lazima nisajili VAT?
answer_sw: Kama CPA aliyesajiliwa, SHUGHULI ZAKO ZA UHASIBU zinastahili usajili wa VAT bila kujali mapato — hii imethibitishwa na TRA. Kwa duka lako la nguo kama biashara TOFAUTI isiyohusiana: kizingiti cha kawaida cha TZS 200M kwa miezi 12 au TZS 100M kwa miezi 6 kinatumika kwa biashara hiyo tofauti. Leseni yako ya CPA haifanyi usajili wa VAT wa lazima kwa biashara zako zote ambazo hazihusiani na uhasibu. Hata hivyo, shughuli zote lazima ziorodheshwe kwa TRA — thibitisha hali yako maalum ya pamoja na TRA au mshauri wa kodi aliyehitimu. Hata kama ungekuwa tu mfanyabiashara wa nguo bila leseni ya CPA, ungepaswa pia kusajili VAT ukifikia kizingiti cha TZS 200M. Kwa hali yako, usajili ni wa lazima haraka.
question_en: My ordinary business (clothing shop) has not reached TZS 200M. But I am also a CPA. Must I register for VAT?
answer_en: As a registered CPA, your PROFESSIONAL ACCOUNTING SERVICES activity requires immediate VAT registration regardless of fees earned — this is confirmed by TRA. For your clothing shop as a SEPARATE unrelated business: the standard threshold of TZS 200M per 12 months or TZS 100M per 6 months applies to that business independently. Your CPA registration does not automatically extend mandatory VAT registration to your unrelated clothing business. However, both activities must be declared to TRA — confirm your specific combined situation with TRA or a qualified tax adviser. Even if you were just a clothing trader without a CPA licence, you would need to register for VAT once reaching the TZS 200M threshold. In your situation, registration is immediately mandatory.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Kwa muhtasari: biashara ya kawaida VS fani iliyodhibitiwa — tofauti yao katika VAT ni nini?
answer_sw: Tofauti kuu: BIASHARA YA KAWAIDA — usajili wa VAT ni wa lazima tu ukifika kizingiti cha TZS 200M kwa miezi 12 au TZS 100M kwa miezi 6. FANI ZILIZODHIBITIWA (wakili, CPA, mhandisi, daktari, msanifu majengo) — usajili wa VAT ni wa lazima MARA MOJA ukipata leseni ya kitaalamu, bila kujali mauzo. Hakuna kizingiti cha mauzo kwa fani zilizodhibitiwa — zinahitaji kusajiliwa mapema.
question_en: Summary: ordinary business VS regulated profession — what is the difference for VAT?
answer_en: Key difference: ORDINARY BUSINESS — VAT registration is mandatory only when reaching TZS 200M per 12 months or TZS 100M per 6 months threshold. REGULATED PROFESSIONS (lawyer, CPA, engineer, doctor, architect) — VAT registration is mandatory IMMEDIATELY upon obtaining a professional licence, regardless of income. There is no income threshold for regulated professions — they must register early.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Kizingiti cha VAT cha miezi 6 ni TZS ngapi — ni sawa na kizingiti cha miezi 12?
answer_sw: Hapana — viwango ni tofauti. Kizingiti cha miezi 12: TZS 200,000,000 (milioni 200). Kizingiti cha miezi 6: TZS 100,000,000 (milioni 100) tu. Si kizingiti kimoja cha TZS 200M kinachotumika kwa njia zote mbili. Kizingiti cha miezi 6 ni nusu ya cha miezi 12. Kila kimoja kinafanya kazi kwa njia yake: ukizidi MOJA tu kati ya viwango hivi viwili, usajili wa VAT ni wa lazima mara moja.
question_en: What is the 6-month VAT threshold — is it the same as the 12-month threshold?
answer_en: No — the thresholds are different. 12-month threshold: TZS 200,000,000 (200 million). 6-month threshold: TZS 100,000,000 (100 million) only. It is not one threshold of TZS 200M applied in both ways. The 6-month threshold is half of the 12-month one. Each works independently: if you exceed EITHER ONE of these two thresholds, VAT registration is immediately mandatory.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax
next_review_trigger: Finance Act amendment changing VAT registration thresholds

question_sw: Mauzo yangu ni TZS 110M katika miezi 6 lakini TZS 160M kwa miezi 12. Je, lazima nisajili VAT?
answer_sw: NDIYO — lazima usajili VAT. Hata kama mauzo ya miezi 12 (TZS 160M) hayajafika kizingiti cha TZS 200M, mauzo yako ya miezi 6 (TZS 110M) yamezidi kizingiti cha TZS 100M. Viwango viwili vinafanya kazi kwa UHURU — kuzidi kimoja kimoja kunafanya usajili kuwa wa lazima mara moja. Katika hali yako, kizingiti cha miezi 6 kimezidiwa — usajili wa VAT ni wa lazima leo.
question_en: My sales are TZS 110M in 6 months but TZS 160M over 12 months. Must I register for VAT?
answer_en: YES — you must register for VAT. Even if the 12-month sales (TZS 160M) have not reached the TZS 200M threshold, your 6-month sales (TZS 110M) have exceeded the TZS 100M threshold. The two thresholds work INDEPENDENTLY — exceeding either one individually makes registration immediately mandatory. In your situation the 6-month threshold has been exceeded — VAT registration is mandatory today.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Je, kizingiti cha miezi 6 cha TZS 100M kinatumika kwa miezi sita MAALUM (Jan-Jun) au kipindi chochote?
answer_sw: Kizingiti cha miezi 6 kinatumika kwa KIPINDI CHOCHOTE cha miezi 6 mfululizo — si kwa miezi sita maalum ya mwaka. Hii inamaanisha TRA inaangalia mauzo yako katika kipindi cha kuzunguka (rolling 6-month period). Mauzo ya miezi Januari-Juni, Februari-Julai, Machi-Agosti — yote yanachaguliwa. Ukizidi TZS 100M katika kipindi chochote cha miezi 6, usajili ni wa lazima.
question_en: Does the 6-month TZS 100M threshold apply to SPECIFIC months (Jan-Jun) or any 6-month period?
answer_en: The 6-month threshold applies to ANY consecutive 6-month period — not specific calendar months. This means TRA looks at your sales in a rolling 6-month period. Sales for January-June, February-July, March-August — all are considered. If you exceed TZS 100M in any 6-month period at all, registration is mandatory.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Rafiki yangu alisema kizingiti cha VAT cha miezi 6 pia ni TZS 200M — kweli au uwongo?
answer_sw: UWONGO — rafiki yako ana kosa. Kizingiti cha miezi 6 ni TZS 100,000,000 (milioni MIA), si TZS 200M. Kizingiti cha TZS 200M ni cha miezi 12 tu. Makosa kama haya yanaweza kusababisha biashara nyingi kukosa usajili wa VAT waliotakiwa — TRA inaweza kutoza adhabu za kodi na faida kwa kipindi chote ambacho biashara ilikimbia usajili.
question_en: My friend said the 6-month VAT threshold is also TZS 200M — true or false?
answer_en: FALSE — your friend is mistaken. The 6-month threshold is TZS 100,000,000 (one hundred million), not TZS 200M. The TZS 200M threshold applies only to the 12-month period. Errors like this can cause many businesses to miss required VAT registration — TRA may charge tax penalties and interest for the entire period during which the business evaded registration.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Kwa muhtasari: viwango vya VAT Tanzania ni vipi?
answer_sw: Viwango VYA LAZIMA (mandatory) vya usajili wa VAT Tanzania: (1) TZS 200,000,000 katika KIPINDI CHOCHOTE cha miezi 12 mfululizo; AU (2) TZS 100,000,000 katika KIPINDI CHOCHOTE cha miezi 6 mfululizo. Moja tu ya viwango hivi kuzidiwa kunafanya usajili kuwa wa lazima mara moja. Fani zilizodhibitiwa (wakili, CPA, nk) lazima zisajilishwe mara moja bila kujali mauzo. Pia: unaweza kusajili VAT kwa hiari hata kama hujafika viwango hivi.
question_en: Summary: what are Tanzania's VAT registration thresholds?
answer_en: MANDATORY VAT registration thresholds in Tanzania: (1) TZS 200,000,000 in ANY consecutive 12-month period; OR (2) TZS 100,000,000 in ANY consecutive 6-month period. Exceeding either one of these thresholds alone makes registration immediately mandatory. Regulated professions (lawyers, CPAs, etc.) must register immediately regardless of sales. Also: you may voluntarily register for VAT even if you have not reached these thresholds.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Nilikuwa na mauzo ya TZS 90M kwa miezi 6 na TZS 185M kwa miezi 12. Je, ninahitaji kusajili VAT?
answer_sw: Hapana — bado haujafika kizingiti. Mauzo ya TZS 90M kwa miezi 6 ni chini ya kizingiti cha TZS 100M cha miezi 6. Mauzo ya TZS 185M kwa miezi 12 ni chini ya kizingiti cha TZS 200M cha miezi 12. Viwango vyote viwili havijazidiwa — kwa hivyo usajili wa VAT wa lazima haujafika. Hata hivyo, angalia kipindi kinachofuata — ukiwa karibu na viwango, zingatia usajili wa hiari au panga vizuri.
question_en: I had sales of TZS 90M over 6 months and TZS 185M over 12 months. Do I need to register for VAT?
answer_en: No — you have not yet reached either threshold. Sales of TZS 90M over 6 months are below the TZS 100M 6-month threshold. Sales of TZS 185M over 12 months are below the TZS 200M 12-month threshold. Neither threshold has been exceeded — so mandatory VAT registration has not been triggered. However, watch the next period — if you are close, consider voluntary registration or careful planning.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Mauzo yangu yalifika TZS 201M kwa miezi 12 — hatua yangu ya kwanza ni nini?
answer_sw: Hatua ya KWANZA mara moja: WASILIANA NA TRA na anza mchakato wa usajili wa VAT. Usiendelee kufanya biashara bila VAT ukisha kuzidi kizingiti — kila siku ya kuchelewa ni siku ya kukiuka sheria. TRA inaweza kutoza adhabu za VAT yote iliyopaswa kulipwa tangu ulipozidi kizingiti, pamoja na faida ya kuchelewa. Usisubiri mwisho wa mwezi au mwaka — hatua ya kwanza ni kuwasiliana na TRA MARA MOJA.
question_en: My sales have reached TZS 201M over 12 months — what is my first step?
answer_en: Your FIRST step immediately: CONTACT TRA and start the VAT registration process. Do not continue trading without VAT once you have exceeded the threshold — every day of delay is a day of violating the law. TRA may charge penalties for all VAT that should have been paid since you crossed the threshold, plus late payment interest. Do not wait until end of month or year — the first step is to contact TRA IMMEDIATELY.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Biashara yangu ina msimu wa biashara (seasonal business) — mauzo yangu ya majira ya kiangazi ni TZS 130M kwa miezi 4. Je, lazima nisajili VAT?
answer_sw: Hata kama ni biashara ya msimu, ukizidi TZS 100M katika kipindi chochote cha miezi 6 — au TZS 200M katika kipindi chochote cha miezi 12 — usajili wa VAT ni wa lazima. Mauzo ya TZS 130M kwa miezi 4 ni mauzo ya haraka sana. Angalia kama katika kipindi chochote cha miezi 6 unaathiriwa na msimu huo mauzo yanazidi TZS 100M — kama ndivyo, usajili ni wa lazima. Msimu wa biashara haukuepusha na sheria ya VAT.
question_en: My business is seasonal — my summer sales are TZS 130M over 4 months. Must I register for VAT?
answer_en: Even if it is a seasonal business, if you exceed TZS 100M in any 6-month period — or TZS 200M in any 12-month period — VAT registration is mandatory. Sales of TZS 130M over 4 months is a very high rate. Check whether in any 6-month period affected by that season the sales exceed TZS 100M — if so, registration is mandatory. Seasonal trading does not exempt you from VAT law.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Ninashiriki mauzo pamoja na mwangu (joint business) — mauzo ya kila mmoja wetu yanashughulikiwa tofauti kwa VAT?
answer_sw: Inategemea muundo wa kisheria wa biashara. Kama mnafanya kazi kama biashara MOJA iliyosajiliwa pamoja — mauzo yanaunganishwa na kizingiti kinahesabiwa kwa biashara nzima. Kama kila mmoja ana biashara YAKE iliyosajiliwa tofauti (kwa TIN tofauti) — kizingiti kinachaguliwa kwa kila biashara tofauti. Mgawanyo bandia wa biashara moja kuepuka VAT ni haramu — TRA inaweza kuunganisha biashara kama ikiamua mfumo wa mgawanyo ni wa kubuni.
question_en: I share a business with my son (joint business) — are each of our sales treated separately for VAT?
answer_en: It depends on the legal structure of the business. If you operate as ONE jointly registered business — sales are combined and the threshold is calculated for the whole business. If each has their OWN separately registered business (with different TINs) — the threshold is assessed for each business separately. Artificial splitting of one business to avoid VAT is illegal — TRA may consolidate businesses if it determines the split is fabricated.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Kuna viwango VIWILI vya usajili wa VAT Tanzania — taja vyote viwili kwa usahihi.
answer_sw: Viwango VYA LAZIMA vya usajili wa VAT Tanzania ni viwili: (1) Kizingiti cha MIEZI 12: mauzo yanayozidi TZS 200,000,000 katika kipindi chochote cha miezi 12 mfululizo; (2) Kizingiti cha MIEZI 6: mauzo yanayozidi TZS 100,000,000 katika kipindi chochote cha miezi 6 mfululizo. Kama kizingiti KIMOJA tu kati ya hivi viwili kimezidiwa, usajili wa VAT ni wa lazima mara moja — huhitajiki kuzidi vyote viwili.
question_en: There are TWO VAT registration thresholds in Tanzania — state both accurately.
answer_en: Tanzania's TWO mandatory VAT registration thresholds are: (1) 12-MONTH threshold: sales exceeding TZS 200,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; (2) 6-MONTH threshold: sales exceeding TZS 100,000,000 in any consecutive 6-month period. If EITHER ONE of these thresholds is exceeded, VAT registration is immediately mandatory — you do not need to exceed both.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax
next_review_trigger: Finance Act amendment changing VAT registration thresholds

question_sw: Biashara yangu inatoa huduma za exempt (zisizo na VAT). Je, naweza kudai mkopo wa VAT ya pembejeo?
answer_sw: HAPANA — hii ni kanuni ngumu bila ubaguzi. Ukitoa huduma au bidhaa za EXEMPT, huwezi kudai mkopo wa VAT ya pembejeo (input VAT) inayohusiana na huduma hizo. Hii ndiyo tofauti kuu kati ya exempt na zero-rated: zero-rated = unalipishwa VAT 0% LAKINI unaweza kudai input VAT; exempt = haulipishwi VAT NA huwezi kudai input VAT. Kwa biashara za exempt, gharama za VAT za pembejeo ni gharama za biashara — hazirudi.
question_en: My business provides exempt (non-VAT) services. Can I claim input VAT credits?
answer_en: NO — this is a hard rule with no exceptions. If you supply EXEMPT services or goods, you cannot claim input VAT credits related to those exempt supplies. This is the key difference between exempt and zero-rated: zero-rated = you charge 0% VAT AND you can claim input VAT; exempt = you do not charge VAT AND you cannot claim input VAT. For exempt businesses, input VAT costs are business expenses — they do not come back.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Ninafanya biashara ya exempt — 'kwa ujumla' naweza kudai input VAT au si?
answer_sw: Hapana — si 'kwa ujumla' bali KAMWE. Kanuni ya exempt haibadiliki: kama biashara yako ina asili ya exempt, huwezi kudai input VAT inayohusiana na biashara hiyo. Lugha ya hedging kama 'kwa ujumla' au 'inategemea hali' si sahihi kwa kanuni hii — ni kanuni ngumu (hard rule) ya sheria ya VAT Tanzania. Ikiwa una biashara zote mbili (exempt na taxable), unaweza kudai input VAT ya sehemu ya taxable tu — si ya sehemu ya exempt.
question_en: I run an exempt business — 'in general' can I claim input VAT or not?
answer_en: No — not 'in general' but NEVER. The exempt rule does not change: if your business is exempt in nature, you cannot claim input VAT related to that business. Hedging language like 'in general' or 'it depends on the situation' is not accurate for this rule — it is a hard rule in Tanzanian VAT law. If you have both (exempt and taxable) activities, you may claim input VAT for the taxable portion only — not for the exempt portion.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Biashara yangu haijasajiliwa VAT — lakini ninaweka VAT ya 18% kwenye invoice zangu kwa sababu wateja wanauliza. Je, hii inaruhusiwa?
answer_sw: HAPANA — hii ni kinyume kabisa cha sheria. Ni biashara zilizosajiliwa VAT TU ambazo zinaruhusiwa kukusanya VAT na kuitoa kwenye invoice. Biashara isiyosajiliwa VAT inayoweka VAT kwenye invoice inafanya vitendo viwili visivyo halali: (1) inakusanya pesa ambazo si yake kisheria na si zake kwa wateja; (2) inaweza kutoa 'input VAT credit ya uwongo' kwa wateja wanaotaka kudai mkopo. TRA inaweza kushtaki biashara kama hiyo na kutoza adhabu kali.
question_en: My business is not VAT registered — but I put 18% VAT on my invoices because clients ask for it. Is this permitted?
answer_en: NO — this is completely against the law. Only VAT-REGISTERED businesses are permitted to charge VAT and show it on invoices. An unregistered business putting VAT on invoices commits two unlawful acts: (1) it is collecting money it is not legally entitled to from clients; (2) it may be issuing 'false input VAT credits' to clients who want to claim credits. TRA may prosecute such a business and impose severe penalties.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: 'Mnunuzi anayehitimu' (qualifying buyer) kwa VAT withholding ni nani hasa — ni mtu yeyote aliyesajili VAT?
answer_sw: Hapana — 'mnunuzi anayehitimu' (qualifying buyer) si mtu yeyote aliyesajili VAT. Qualifying buyer ni: (a) Wizara za Serikali na taasisi za serikali; (b) taasisi zinazohifadhi mapato yake mwenyewe (self-accounting entities); au (c) mtu aliyeteuliwa rasmi na Kamishna Mkuu wa TRA kama wakala wa zuio la VAT (designated VAT withholding agent). Kampuni ya kawaida iliyosajili VAT si qualifying buyer — haiwezi kuzuia VAT ya wasambazaji wake bila uteuzi maalum wa TRA.
question_en: Who exactly is a 'qualifying buyer' for VAT withholding — is it anyone who has registered for VAT?
answer_en: No — a 'qualifying buyer' is not anyone who has registered for VAT. A qualifying buyer is: (a) Government ministries and government institutions; (b) self-accounting entities; or (c) a person formally designated by the TRA Commissioner General as a designated VAT withholding agent. An ordinary company that has registered for VAT is NOT a qualifying buyer — it cannot withhold VAT from its suppliers without a specific TRA designation.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax
next_review_trigger: Finance Act amendment changing qualifying buyer definition

question_sw: Je, serikali ya mtaa (manispaa) inaweza kuzuia VAT kwenye malipo yake kwa wasambazaji?
answer_sw: NDIYO — serikali za mitaa, manispaa, na taasisi za serikali zote ni 'qualifying buyers' ambazo zinaweza kuzuia VAT. Zinazuia: (a) asilimia 3 ya VAT kwenye malipo ya bidhaa, au (b) asilimia 6 ya VAT kwenye malipo ya huduma. Serikali au taasisi lazima itoe hati ya zuio la VAT kwa msambazaji siku ambayo VAT inastahili kulipwa — si tarehe ya 20 ya mwezi.
question_en: Can a local government (municipality) withhold VAT from its payments to suppliers?
answer_en: YES — local governments, municipalities, and all government institutions are 'qualifying buyers' that can withhold VAT. They withhold: (a) 3% VAT on goods payments, or (b) 6% VAT on services payments. The government or institution must issue a VAT withholding certificate to the supplier on the day the VAT becomes payable — not on the 20th of the month.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Nilizidi kizingiti cha VAT wiki hii — hatua ya KWANZA ninayopaswa kuchukua ni nini?
answer_sw: Hatua ya KWANZA ni KUWASILIANA NA TRA MARA MOJA na kuomba usajili wa VAT. Usiendelee kufanya biashara bila VAT baada ya kuzidi kizingiti — hii ni ukiukaji wa sheria ya kodi. USIFANYE: (1) usiwasilishe 'return ya mwisho' (final VAT return) — hii ni ya usimamizi wa VAT uliopo, si ya kuanza usajili mpya; (2) usisubiri mwezi mzima au mwaka — muda wa kuchelewa ni gharama ya adhabu. Nenda TRA leo.
question_en: I exceeded the VAT threshold this week — what is the FIRST step I should take?
answer_en: The FIRST step is to CONTACT TRA IMMEDIATELY and apply for VAT registration. Do not continue trading without VAT after exceeding the threshold — this is a tax law violation. DO NOT: (1) do not submit a 'final VAT return' — that is for winding up an existing VAT registration, not starting a new one; (2) do not wait a full month or year — delay time is penalty cost. Go to TRA today.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Baada ya kuzidi kizingiti cha VAT, ninaweza kuendelea kufanya biashara wakati wa kusubiri TRA kunisajili?
answer_sw: Unaweza kuendelea na biashara LAKINI lazima uanze kutunza kumbukumbu za mauzo yako vizuri kuanzia siku uliyozidi kizingiti. Kwa vitendo: huwezi kukusanya VAT rasmi kutoka kwa wateja mpaka usajili ukamilike — lakini unastahili kufanya hivyo baada ya usajili. TRA inaweza kukuambia ulipe VAT ya kipindi chote tangu ulipozidi kizingiti hata kabla ya usajili rasmi. Inashauriwa: funga mauzo mapya mpya baada ya kusajilishwa.
question_en: After exceeding the VAT threshold, can I continue trading while waiting for TRA to register me?
answer_en: You may continue trading BUT you must start keeping careful sales records from the day you exceeded the threshold. Practically: you cannot formally collect VAT from customers until registration is complete — but you should do so after registration. TRA may ask you to pay VAT for the entire period since you exceeded the threshold even before formal registration. Advisable: apply proper VAT from the date of registration.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Adhabu ya biashara isiyosajiliwa VAT inayokusanya VAT ni nini?
answer_sw: Biashara isiyosajiliwa inayokusanya VAT inaweza kukabiliwa na adhabu kama vile: (1) kurudisha VAT yote iliyokusanywa kwa TRA bila kupewa mkopo wowote wa pembejeo; (2) faini za kodi za ziada kwa ukiukaji wa makusudi; (3) kuzuiwa kwa biashara hadi kusajilishwa. Pia: wateja waliodai input VAT kutoka biashara isiyosajiliwa wanaweza kukabiliwa na marekebisho ya kodi — TRA inaweza kukataa madai yao.
question_en: What is the penalty for an unregistered business that collects VAT?
answer_en: An unregistered business collecting VAT may face penalties such as: (1) remitting all collected VAT to TRA without receiving any input VAT credit; (2) additional tax penalties for deliberate violation; (3) business closure until registration. Also: customers who claimed input VAT from the unregistered business may face tax assessments — TRA may reject their claims.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Wakati wa VAT withholding — TRA inasema hati ya zuio lazima itolewa 'tarehe ya 20'. Ni kweli?
answer_sw: HAPANA — hii ni kosa maarufu. Hati ya zuio la VAT (VAT withholding certificate) lazima itolewa SIKU AMBAYO VAT INASTAHILI KULIPWA — si tarehe ya 20. Tarehe ya 20 ni tarehe ya kuwasilisha RETURN ya VAT na kulipa VAT — hii ni wajibu tofauti kabisa. Zuio la VAT na utoaji wa hati lazima ufanyike wakati wa malipo au siku VAT inastahili — si mwezi mzima baadaye.
question_en: For VAT withholding — TRA says the withholding certificate must be issued by 'the 20th'. Is this correct?
answer_en: NO — this is a common error. A VAT withholding certificate must be issued on THE DAY THE VAT BECOMES PAYABLE — not the 20th. The 20th is the date for submitting the VAT RETURN and paying VAT — this is a completely separate obligation. VAT withholding and certificate issuance must happen at the time of payment or when VAT becomes due — not a full month later.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Tofauti kati ya tarehe ya 20 (VAT return) na tarehe ya hati ya zuio la VAT?
answer_sw: Tarehe MBILI tofauti: (1) TAREHE YA 20 ya kila mwezi: hii ni mwisho wa kuwasilisha return ya VAT (VAT return) na kulipa VAT unayodaiwa. Inahusu biashara yoyote iliyosajiliwa VAT. (2) TAREHE YA KUTOA HATI YA ZUIO: hii ni siku ambayo VAT inastahili kulipwa — si mwishoni mwa mwezi. Inahusu manunuzi anayehitimu (qualifying buyer) anayezuia VAT. Kufanya kazi kama qualifying buyer na kutoa hati tarehe ya 20 ni kuchelewa — lazima itolewa mara tu wakati wa zuio.
question_en: What is the difference between the 20th (VAT return) and the VAT withholding certificate date?
answer_en: TWO different dates: (1) THE 20TH of each month: this is the deadline for submitting a VAT return and paying the VAT owed. It applies to any VAT-registered business. (2) VAT WITHHOLDING CERTIFICATE DATE: this is the day the VAT becomes payable — not at month end. It applies to a qualifying buyer who withholds VAT. Operating as a qualifying buyer and issuing certificates on the 20th is late — they must be issued immediately at the time of withholding.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Ninajua biashara yangu itafika kizingiti cha VAT mwezi ujao. Ninaweza kusajili leo kabla ya kufika?
answer_sw: Ndiyo — unaweza kusajili VAT kwa HIARI kabla ya kufika kizingiti. Hii inaitwa usajili wa hiari (voluntary registration). Faida: unaweza kuanza kudai mkopo wa VAT ya pembejeo mara moja, na wateja wako wa biashara wanaweza kudai input VAT kutoka kwa mahesabu yako. Usajili wa hiari unakufanya uanze kupeleka return ya kila mwezi na kukusanya VAT tangu tarehe ya usajili — si kipindi cha nyuma.
question_en: I know my business will reach the VAT threshold next month. Can I register today before reaching it?
answer_en: Yes — you can register for VAT VOLUNTARILY before reaching the threshold. This is called voluntary registration. Benefit: you can start claiming input VAT credits immediately, and your business clients can claim input VAT from your invoices. Voluntary registration means you start submitting monthly returns and collecting VAT from the registration date — not for any past period.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Biashara yangu ina mauzo ya taxable NA ya exempt pamoja. Ninaweza kudai input VAT yote?
answer_sw: Unaweza kudai input VAT ya SEHEMU YA TAXABLE tu. Kwa biashara zenye mchanganyiko wa taxable na exempt, TRA inatumia kanuni ya 'partial attribution' — unagawanya input VAT kulingana na uwiano wa mauzo ya taxable kwa mauzo yote. Mfano: kama 70% ya mauzo ni taxable na 30% exempt, unaweza kudai 70% ya input VAT yako tu. Sehemu ya 30% inayohusiana na mauzo ya exempt hairejeshwi.
question_en: My business has both taxable AND exempt sales. Can I claim all input VAT?
answer_en: You can claim input VAT for the TAXABLE PORTION only. For businesses with a mix of taxable and exempt supplies, TRA applies a 'partial attribution' rule — you apportion input VAT based on the ratio of taxable sales to total sales. Example: if 70% of sales are taxable and 30% exempt, you may claim 70% of your input VAT only. The 30% portion related to exempt supplies is not refunded.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: Ninaweza kukataa ombi la mteja kuzuia VAT kwenye invoice yangu?
answer_sw: Inategemea hali ya mteja wako. Kama mteja ni 'qualifying buyer' (serikali, taasisi ya serikali, au wakala aliyeteuliwa na TRA) — hana chaguo: wana wajibu wa kisheria wa kuzuia VAT. Huwezi kuwakatalia kisheria kuzuia VAT wanapostahili kufanya hivyo. Kama mteja ni kampuni ya kawaida isiyokuwa 'qualifying buyer' — hawana haki ya kuzuia VAT na unaomba kwamba walipe VAT kamili.
question_en: Can I refuse a client's request to withhold VAT on my invoice?
answer_en: It depends on your client's status. If the client is a 'qualifying buyer' (government, government institution, or TRA-designated agent) — there is no choice: they have a legal obligation to withhold VAT. You cannot legally prevent them from withholding VAT when they are required to do so. If the client is an ordinary company that is not a 'qualifying buyer' — they have no right to withhold VAT and you should ask them to pay VAT in full.
primary_source_name: TRA - Value Added Tax

question_sw: TRA inazuia VAT gani kwa malipo ya bidhaa na kwa malipo ya huduma?
answer_sw: VAT withholding ya Tanzania (Finance Act 2025, kuanza Julai 2025): BIDHAA — asilimia 3 ya VAT inazuiwa; HUDUMA — asilimia 6 ya VAT inazuiwa. Tofauti: kiwango cha bidhaa (3%) ni nusu ya kiwango cha huduma (6%). Kumbuka: hizi si viwango vya VAT vyenyewe (ambayo ni 18%) — ni sehemu tu ya VAT inayozuiwa na qualifying buyer kabla ya kufikia msambazaji.
question_en: What VAT withholding rate does TRA apply to goods payments and services payments?
answer_en: Tanzania VAT withholding (Finance Act 2025, effective July 2025): GOODS — 3% VAT is withheld; SERVICES — 6% VAT is withheld. The difference: the goods rate (3%) is half the services rate (6%). Note: these are not the VAT rates themselves (which are 18%) — they are only the portion of VAT withheld by the qualifying buyer before it reaches the supplier.

question_sw: Kwa muhtasari — kanuni ngumu tatu za VAT ambazo kila mfanyabiashara lazima azijue.
answer_sw: Kanuni tatu ngumu (hard rules) za VAT Tanzania: (1) EXEMPT = HAKUNA input VAT — ukitoa huduma/bidhaa za exempt, huwezi kudai input VAT inayohusiana nazo, bila ubaguzi; (2) USAJILI WA LAZIMA MARA MOJA — ukizidi kizingiti cha TZS 200M/miezi 12 au TZS 100M/miezi 6, wasiliana na TRA leo — usichelewesha; (3) BIASHARA ISIYOSAJILIWA HAIKUSANYI VAT — ni kinyume cha sheria kuweka VAT kwenye invoice kama hujasajiliwa.
question_en: Summary — three hard VAT rules every business person must know.
answer_en: Three hard rules of Tanzanian VAT: (1) EXEMPT = NO input VAT — if you supply exempt services/goods, you cannot claim related input VAT, no exceptions; (2) MANDATORY IMMEDIATE REGISTRATION — if you exceed TZS 200M/12 months or TZS 100M/6 months threshold, contact TRA today — do not delay; (3) UNREGISTERED BUSINESS DOES NOT CHARGE VAT — it is against the law to put VAT on invoices if you are not registered.

question_sw: Bendi ya pili ya PAYE Tanzania ni asilimia 9 — ni kweli?
answer_sw: UWONGO — bendi ya pili ya PAYE ni asilimia 8, si 9. Bendi zote tano za PAYE kwa kipindi cha 2025/2026: Bendi 1: TZS 0-270,000 = 0%; Bendi 2: TZS 270,001-520,000 = 8%; Bendi 3: TZS 520,001-760,000 = 20%; Bendi 4: TZS 760,001-1,000,000 = 25%; Bendi 5: Zaidi ya TZS 1,000,000 = 30%. Kizingiti cha mapato yasiyotozwa kodi: TZS 3,240,000 kwa mwaka (TZS 270,000/mwezi kwa kiwango cha 0%, imejengwa ndani ya Bendi 1). Kumbuka: bendi ya 2 ni 8% — si 9% — kosa hili ni la kawaida.
question_en: The second PAYE band in Tanzania is 9% — is this true?
answer_en: FALSE — the second PAYE band is 8%, not 9%. All five PAYE bands for 2025/2026: Band 1: TZS 0-270,000 = 0%; Band 2: TZS 270,001-520,000 = 8%; Band 3: TZS 520,001-760,000 = 20%; Band 4: TZS 760,001-1,000,000 = 25%; Band 5: Above TZS 1,000,000 = 30%. Annual tax-free threshold: TZS 3,240,000 (TZS 270,000/month at 0%, built into Band 1). Remember: band 2 is 8% — not 9% — this error is very common.

question_sw: Bendi za PAYE za Tanzania kwa mwaka 2025/2026 ni zipi — zitaje zote tano kwa usahihi?

Kodi inazingatiwa kwenye KIPATO KINACHOPITA kizingiti cha kila bendi — si kwenye mshahara wote.
question_en: What are Tanzania's PAYE bands for 2025/2026 — list all five accurately?
answer_en: Five PAYE bands for Tanzania 2025/2026: (1) TZS 0 to 270,000: rate 0%; (2) TZS 270,001 to 520,000: rate 8% (not 9%); (3) TZS 520,001 to 760,000: rate 20%; (4) TZS 760,001 to 1,000,000: rate 25%; (5) Above TZS 1,000,000: rate 30%. Monthly Annual tax-free threshold: TZS 3,240,000/year (TZS 270,000/month at 0% — built into Band 1, no separate monthly relief).. Tax applies to income ABOVE each band threshold — not on the total salary.

question_sw: Mhesabu wangu alisema bendi ya 2 ya PAYE ni asilimia 9. Je, ana haki?

question_sw: PAYE inafanya kazi vipi — inatumika kwenye mshahara wote au kwa bendi?
answer_sw: PAYE inafanya kazi KWA BENDI (progressive taxation) — si kwenye mshahara wote kwa kiwango kimoja. Mfano wa mshahara wa TZS 600,000: Bendi 1 (0-270,000): TZS 0 kodi; Bendi 2 (270,001-520,000): TZS 250,000 × 8% = TZS 20,000; Bendi 3 (520,001-600,000): TZS 80,000 × 20% = TZS 16,000; Jumla ya PAYE: TZS 36,000. Kumbuka: PAYE Tanzania haina punguzo la kibinafsi tofauti la kila mwezi linalotakiwa kukatwa — kiwango cha sifuri hadi TZS 270,000 ndiyo ruhusa pekee iliyojengwa ndani ya mfumo. Kwa mahesabu ya mshahara mahususi tumia TRA IDRAS (taidras.tra.go.tz). Tafadhali tumia TRA IDRAS kwa mahesabu sahihi ya mshahara wako.
question_en: How does PAYE work — does it apply to the full salary or by band?
answer_en: PAYE works BY BAND (progressive taxation) — not on the full salary at one rate. Example for TZS 600,000 salary: Band 1 (0-270,000): TZS 0 tax; Band 2 (270,001-520,000): TZS 250,000 × 8% = TZS 20,000; Band 3 (520,001-600,000): TZS 80,000 × 20% = TZS 16,000; Total PAYE: TZS 36,000. Note: Tanzania's PAYE has no separate monthly personal relief deduction — the zero-rate up to TZS 270,000 is the only built-in allowance. For specific salary calculations use TRA IDRAS (taidras.tra.go.tz). Please use TRA IDRAS for accurate calculations for your specific salary.

question_sw: Punguzo la kibinafsi la PAYE Tanzania ni TZS ngapi kwa mwezi?

Hakuna punguzo la kibinafsi tofauti la TZS 26,000 kwa mwezi linalotakiwa kukatwa kutoka PAYE iliyohesabiwa. Mapato yanayozidi TZS 270,000 yanatozwa kodi kwa msururu wa 8% kuanzia. Kwa mahesabu sahihi ya PAYE ya mshahara wako mahususi: tumia TRA IDRAS (taidras.tra.go.tz) au msaada wa mhesabu wa kodi aliyehitimu.

answer_en: Tanzania's PAYE system has a zero-rate band for the first TZS 270,000 of monthly income — this is the built-in tax-free allowance. There is no separate monthly personal relief of TZS 26,000 to subtract from calculated PAYE. Income above TZS 270,000 is taxed progressively starting at 8%. For accurate PAYE calculations for your specific salary: use TRA IDRAS (taidras.tra.go.tz) or the services of a qualified tax accountant.

question_en: Salary of TZS 270,001 (one shilling above the threshold) — does the employee pay PAYE?
answer_en: Yes — a salary of TZS 270,001 is affected by the second PAYE band. But: tax applies to the portion exceeding the TZS 270,000 threshold only — not the full salary. TZS 1 × 8% = TZS 0.08. This is effectively zero in any practical sense — the total PAYE generated at this income level is negligible. Note: there is no separate TZS 26,000 monthly personal relief deduction in Tanzania's PAYE system. In practice: an employee will not pay PAYE until their salary reaches the level where PAYE bands generate PAYE exceeding TZS 26,000.

question_sw: Mwajiri alitumia mfumo wa zamani wa PAYE unaotumia bendi ya 9%. Wafanyakazi wanapaswa kupata rejesho la ziada waliyolipa?
answer_sw: Ndiyo — ikiwa mfumo ulitumia 9% badala ya 8% kwa bendi ya pili, mfanyakazi alikuwa akilipa PAYE zaidi ya inayostahili. Tofauti ni 1% ya mapato kati ya TZS 270,001 na TZS 520,000. Mfanyakazi anastahili rejesho la ziada iliyolipwa. Mwajiri anapaswa: (1) kuhesabu tofauti; (2) kuomba TRA marekebisho (amendment) au rejesho (refund); (3) kusasisha mfumo wa mishahara kwa bendi sahihi za 2025/2026.
question_en: An employer used an old PAYE system using a 9% band 2 rate. Are employees entitled to a refund of excess paid?
answer_en: Yes — if the system used 9% instead of 8% for the second band, the employee was paying more PAYE than required. The difference is 1% of income between TZS 270,001 and TZS 520,000. The employee is entitled to a refund of the excess paid. The employer should: (1) calculate the difference; (2) apply to TRA for an amendment or refund; (3) update the payroll system to the correct 2025/2026 bands.

question_en: What is the rate of the third PAYE band (TZS 520,001-760,000)?
answer_en: The third PAYE band in Tanzania is 20%. All five band rates: Band 1 (0-270K): 0%; Band 2 (270K-520K): 8%; Band 3 (520K-760K): 20%; Band 4 (760K-1M): 25%; Band 5 (above 1M): 30%. The jump from band 2 to band 3 is large — from 8% to 20%. This means an employee earning TZS 521,000 pays 8% on the band 2 portion AND 20% on TZS 1,000 in band 3.

answer_sw: Ninajua viwango vya PAYE Tanzania vizuri (bendi 1: 0%; bendi 2: 8%; bendi 3: 20%; bendi 4: 25%; bendi 5: 30%; Kizingiti cha mapato yasiyotozwa kodi: TZS 3,240,000/mwaka (TZS 270,000/mwezi kwa 0% — imejengwa ndani ya Bendi 1, hakuna punguzo tofauti la kila mwezi). lakini mahesabu ya mshahara mahususi yako nje ya mipaka yangu. answer_en: I know Tanzania's PAYE rates well (band 1: 0%; band 2: 8%; band 3: 20%; band 4: 25%; band 5: 30%; Annual tax-free threshold: TZS 3,240,000/year (TZS 270,000/month at 0% — built into Band 1, no separate monthly relief). but specific salary calculations are outside my coverage. Verify with TRA IDRAS (taidras.tra.go.tz) or a qualified tax adviser. For a TZS 900,000 salary, bands 1, 2, 3, and part of band 4 will apply — TRA IDRAS will calculate accurately.

question_sw: Je, bendi za PAYE zinabadilika kila mwaka au zinakaa sawa?
answer_sw: Bendi za PAYE zinaweza kubadilika kila mwaka kupitia Finance Act inayotangazwa kila Julai. Mwaka 2025/2026, bendi ni: Bendi 1 (0-270K): 0%; Bendi 2 (270K-520K): 8%; Bendi 3 (520K-760K): 20%; Bendi 4 (760K-1M): 25%; Bendi 5 (zaidi ya 1M): 30%. Kizingiti cha mapato yasiyotozwa kodi: TZS 3,240,000/mwaka (TZS 270,000/mwezi kwa 0% — imejengwa ndani ya Bendi 1, hakuna punguzo tofauti la kila mwezi)./mwezi. Angalia Finance Act mpya kila Julai au wasiliana na TRA kuthibitisha bendi za sasa. Usitegemee viwango vya zamani bila kuthibitisha.
question_en: Do PAYE bands change every year or do they remain the same?
answer_en: PAYE bands may change annually through the Finance Act published each July. For 2025/2026, the bands are: Band 1 (0-270K): 0%; Band 2 (270K-520K): 8%; Band 3 (520K-760K): 20%; Band 4 (760K-1M): 25%; Band 5 (above 1M): 30%. Annual tax-free threshold: TZS 3,240,000/year (TZS 270,000/month at 0% — built into Band 1, no separate monthly relief)./month. Check the new Finance Act every July or contact TRA to confirm current bands. Do not rely on old rates without verifying.

question_sw: Bendi ya juu kabisa ya PAYE (30%) inaanza lini — ni kwa mapato yote zaidi ya TZS milioni moja?
answer_sw: Ndiyo — kiwango cha 30% kinatumika kwenye sehemu ya mapato INAYOPITA TZS 1,000,000 kwa mwezi. Mapato ya TZS 0-1,000,000 yanapigwa kodi kwa bendi tofauti (0%, 8%, 20%, 25%). Sehemu inayozidi TZS 1,000,000 tu ndiyo inaathiriwa na 30%. Kwa hivyo mfanyakazi mwenye mshahara wa TZS 1,500,000 atalipa 30% kwenye TZS 500,000 tu (sehemu inayopita TZS 1M), si kwenye TZS 1.5M yote.
question_en: When does the highest PAYE band (30%) start — is it on all income above TZS one million?
answer_en: Yes — the 30% rate applies to the portion of income EXCEEDING TZS 1,000,000 per month. Income from TZS 0 to 1,000,000 is taxed at different bands (0%, 8%, 20%, 25%). Only the portion exceeding TZS 1,000,000 is affected by 30%. So an employee earning TZS 1,500,000 will pay 30% on TZS 500,000 only (the portion above TZS 1M), not on the full TZS 1.5M.
primary_source_name: TRA - Pay As You Earn (PAYE)

question_sw: Kwa muhtasari: bendi TANO za PAYE Tanzania kwa 2025/2026 — zitaje kwa usahihi kamili.
answer_sw: Bendi TANO za PAYE Tanzania 2025/2026 — sahihi kamili: (1) TZS 0 hadi 270,000 = 0%; (2) TZS 270,001 hadi 520,000 = 8% (MUHIMU: si 9%); (3) TZS 520,001 hadi 760,000 = 20%; (4) TZS 760,001 hadi 1,000,000 = 25%; (5) Zaidi ya TZS 1,000,000 = 30%. Kodi ya bendi inahusu sehemu ya mapato ndani ya bendi hiyo tu — si mshahara wote. Kwa mahesabu ya mshahara mahususi: tumia TRA IDRAS (taidras.tra.go.tz).
question_en: Summary: the FIVE PAYE bands for Tanzania 2025/2026 — state them with complete accuracy.
answer_en: FIVE PAYE bands for Tanzania 2025/2026 — complete accuracy: (1) TZS 0 to 270,000 = 0%; (2) TZS 270,001 to 520,000 = 8% (IMPORTANT: not 9%); (3) TZS 520,001 to 760,000 = 20%; (4) TZS 760,001 to 1,000,000 = 25%; (5) Above TZS 1,000,000 = 30%. question_sw: GN 487A na kibali cha kazi (work permit) — ni kitu kimoja au tofauti kabisa?
answer_sw: Ni TOFAUTI KABISA — GN 487A na vibali vya kazi ni mifumo miwili tofauti ya kisheria inayosimamia masuala tofauti: GN 487A = LESENI YA BIASHARA — inazuia wageni kufanya AINA FULANI ZA BIASHARA hata kama wana haki ya kuishi na kufanya kazi Tanzania. Kibali cha kazi = SHERIA YA KAZI — inaruhusu mgeni kufanya kazi ya AJIRA kwa mwajiri wa Tanzania. Mgeni anaweza kuwa na kibali cha kazi halali cha kufanya kazi kama mhandisi mkuu — lakini bado anakiuka GN 487A akijaribu kufungua duka la rejareja.
question_en: GN 487A and a work permit — are they the same thing or completely separate?
answer_en: They are COMPLETELY SEPARATE — GN 487A and work permits are two different legal systems governing different matters: GN 487A = BUSINESS LICENSING — prohibits non-citizens from conducting CERTAIN TYPES OF BUSINESS even if they have the right to live and work in Tanzania. Work permit = LABOUR LAW — allows a non-citizen to do EMPLOYED WORK for a Tanzanian employer. A non-citizen may hold a valid work permit to work as a chief engineer — but still violates GN 487A if they try to open a retail shop.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025

question_sw: Mgeni ana kibali cha kazi cha mwaka mmoja. Je, kibali hiki kimempa ruhusa ya kufanya biashara ya jumla?
answer_sw: Hapana — kibali cha kazi (work permit) kinamruhusu mgeni kufanya kazi kwa MWAJIRI MAALUM katika kazi iliyobainishwa kwenye kibali. Hakiruhusu kufanya biashara huru ya jumla au aina nyingine yoyote iliyopigwa marufuku na GN 487A. Biashara ya jumla imekatazwa wazi na GN 487A — kibali cha kazi hakibadilishi marufuku hii. Mgeni anayetaka kufanya biashara ya jumla Tanzania anahitaji zaidi ya kibali cha kazi — suala hili linahitaji ushauri wa kisheria.
question_en: A non-citizen has a one-year work permit. Does this permit them to conduct wholesale trade?
answer_en: No — a work permit allows a non-citizen to work for a SPECIFIC EMPLOYER in the job specified on the permit. It does not permit independent wholesale trade or any other business category prohibited by GN 487A. Wholesale trade is explicitly prohibited by GN 487A — a work permit does not change this prohibition. A non-citizen wishing to conduct wholesale trade in Tanzania needs more than a work permit — this matter requires legal advice.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025
next_review_trigger: Amendment to GN 487A or work permit regulations

question_sw: Kampuni ya Tanzania inayomilikiwa 100% na mgeni — inaweza kufanya biashara ya rejareja kama kampuni (si kama mtu binafsi)?
answer_sw: Hapana — GN 487A inazuia biashara kwa wageni hata kwa njia ya kampuni. Ikiwa mgeni ndiye mmiliki wa 100% na/au mwenye nguvu za uamuzi wa kampuni inayofanya rejareja — hali hii inachukuliwa ukiukaji wa GN 487A. Muundo wa kampuni (limited liability) si ngao dhidi ya sheria hii. Idara ya Uhamiaji na TRA wanaangalia kwa makini umiliki wa kampuni wakati wa uchunguzi wa GN 487A.
question_en: A Tanzanian company 100% owned by a non-citizen — can it conduct retail trade as a company (not as an individual)?
answer_en: No — GN 487A prohibits businesses by non-citizens even through a company structure. If a non-citizen is 100% owner and/or decision-maker of a company conducting retail trade — this situation is treated as a GN 487A violation. The corporate structure (limited liability) is not a shield against this law. The Immigration Department and TRA scrutinise company ownership closely during GN 487A investigations.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025

question_sw: Kampuni ya kimataifa inayomilikiwa na mgeni ina mkurugenzi (director) Mtanzania. Je, hii inafanya biashara ya rejareja iwe halali?
answer_sw: Si kwa lazima. Kuwa na mkurugenzi Mtanzania kwenye ubao wa kampuni hakutoshi kuzuia tatizo la GN 487A kama mgeni bado ndiye mwenye nguvu za uamuzi za kweli za biashara. Idara ya Uhamiaji inaangalia: Ni nani mwenye hisa nyingi? Ni nani anayefanya maamuzi ya kila siku? Mkurugenzi Mtanzania anayefanya kazi kweli au ni jina tu? Ikiwa mkurugenzi Mtanzania ni wa bandia (nominal director), hali hii inaweza kuzingatiwa mpango wa kukwepa sheria.
question_en: An internationally owned company has a Tanzanian director. Does this make retail trade legal?
answer_en: Not necessarily. Having a Tanzanian director on the board is not sufficient to prevent a GN 487A problem if a non-citizen still holds the real decision-making power in the business. The Immigration Department looks at: Who holds the majority shares? Who makes day-to-day decisions? Is the Tanzanian director genuinely working or only a name? If the Tanzanian director is nominal (name-only), this arrangement may be treated as a scheme to circumvent the law.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025

question_sw: Mgeni anayefanya kazi katika EPZ (Eneo Huru la Usindikaji) — GN 487A inazuia biashara zake pia?
answer_sw: Makampuni ya EPZ (Export Processing Zones) na SEZ (Special Economic Zones) yanaweza kuwa na kanuni tofauti kutokana na makubaliano yao maalum ya kisheria na Serikali ya Tanzania. Suala hili si rahisi kujumuisha — EPZ inasimamiwa na Sheria ya EPZ na TIC (Tanzania Investment Centre) ambayo inaweza kutoa ruhusa maalum. Thibitisha hali ya kampuni yako ya EPZ moja kwa moja na TIC, EPZA (Export Processing Zones Authority), na Idara ya Uhamiaji ili kujua kama na kwa kiasi gani GN 487A inatumika.
question_en: A non-citizen working in an EPZ (Export Processing Zone) — does GN 487A restrict their business too?
answer_en: EPZ (Export Processing Zones) and SEZ (Special Economic Zones) companies may have different rules due to their special legal agreements with the Tanzanian government. This issue is not straightforward to generalise — EPZs are regulated by the EPZ Act and TIC (Tanzania Investment Centre) which may grant special permissions. Verify your specific EPZ company situation directly with TIC, EPZA (Export Processing Zones Authority), and the Immigration Department to know if and to what extent GN 487A applies.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025

question_sw: Mgeni alikamatwa kwa ukiukaji wa GN 487A mara ya pili — kuna adhabu maalum ya mara ya pili (recidivism)?
answer_sw: GN 487A kama inavyosomeka haitaji adhabu maalum ya 'mara ya pili' au mfumo wa recidivism. Kila ukiukaji unashughulikiwa kwa kanuni za kawaida za korti za Tanzania ambazo zinazingatia historia ya mshtakiwa wakati wa kutoa hukumu. Korti inaweza kutoa adhabu kubwa zaidi kwa mgeni mwenye historia ya ukiukaji — lakini hii ni uamuzi wa korti, si sharti la kisheria lililowekwa na GN 487A. Kwa ufafanuzi zaidi: wasiliana na mwanasheria wa kisheria cha Tanzania.
question_en: A non-citizen was caught violating GN 487A a second time — is there a special repeat offender (recidivism) penalty?
answer_en: GN 487A as written does not provide for a specific 'second offence' penalty or recidivism system. Each violation is handled under normal Tanzanian court procedures which consider the defendant's history when sentencing. A court may impose a larger penalty for a non-citizen with a violation history — but this is a court decision, not a legal requirement set by GN 487A itself. For more clarification: contact a Tanzanian legal practitioner.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025
next_review_trigger: Amendment to GN 487A adding recidivism provisions

question_sw: Mgeni ana leseni ya biashara ya Tanzania iliyotolewa na serikali ya mtaa — hii inamkinga dhidi ya GN 487A?
answer_sw: Hapana — leseni ya biashara ya serikali ya mtaa haikinga dhidi ya GN 487A. Serikali za mitaa zina mamlaka ya kutoa leseni za biashara kwa madhumuni ya kawaida ya biashara. Lakini: kutoa leseni ya biashara kwa mgeni na biashara hiyo ikiwa kwenye orodha ya GN 487A ni kosa la utekelezaji wa serikali ya mtaa — haibadilishi adhabu ya shirika la kitaifa la uhamiaji. GN 487A inasimamia Idara ya Uhamiaji — si serikali za mitaa.
question_en: A non-citizen has a business licence issued by local government — does this protect against GN 487A?
answer_en: No — a local government business licence does not protect against GN 487A. Local governments have authority to issue business licences for general business purposes. But: issuing a business licence to a non-citizen for a business on the GN 487A list is a local government enforcement error — it does not change the national immigration authority's penalties. GN 487A is enforced by the Immigration Department — not local governments.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025

question_sw: Mgeni anafanya kazi kama CEO wa kampuni kubwa ya biashara ya jumla. Je, ana tatizo la GN 487A?
answer_sw: Mgeni kama CEO (mfanyakazi wa ajira) wa kampuni inayomilikiwa halisi na Watanzania — hali hii ni tofauti na kufanya biashara mwenyewe. GN 487A inazuia wageni kufanya biashara zilizoorodheshwa — si kwa lazima kufanya kazi kama mfanyakazi wa kampuni ya Watanzania. Hata hivyo: ikiwa mgeni ni CEO na pia mmiliki wa hisa nyingi — inaweza kuzingatiwa kufanya biashara, si kufanya kazi tu. Mstari huu mwembamba unahitaji ushauri wa kisheria kwa hali mahususi.
question_en: A non-citizen works as CEO of a large wholesale trading company. Do they have a GN 487A problem?
answer_en: A non-citizen as CEO (employed worker) of a company genuinely owned by Tanzanians — this situation differs from personally conducting a business. GN 487A prohibits non-citizens from conducting the listed businesses — not necessarily from working as an employee of a Tanzanian-owned company. However: if the non-citizen is CEO AND also majority shareholder — it may be treated as conducting business, not merely working. This fine line requires legal advice for the specific situation.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025
next_review_trigger: Amendment to GN 487A or related case law

question_sw: Tofauti kati ya GN 487A (biashara) na sheria ya kazi (labor law) ni nini kwa mgeni?
answer_sw: Tofauti kuu kwa wageni: GN 487A (biashara): inazuia mgeni KUMILIKI au KUENDESHA biashara fulani. Ni kuhusu BIASHARA ya mgeni mwenyewe. Sheria ya kazi (Work Permit): inaruhusu mgeni kufanya KAZI ya AJIRA kwa kampuni ya Tanzania. Ni kuhusu mgeni kufanya kazi kwa MTU MWINGINE. Mgeni anaweza kuwa na kibali cha kazi halali cha kufanya kazi kama daktari mkuu — lakini akifungua kliniki yake binafsi, anakiuka GN 487A. Hizi ni mifumo miwili tofauti.
question_en: What is the difference between GN 487A (business) and labour law for a non-citizen?
answer_en: Key difference for non-citizens: GN 487A (business): prohibits a non-citizen from OWNING or RUNNING certain businesses. It is about the non-citizen's OWN BUSINESS. Labour law (Work Permit): permits a non-citizen to do EMPLOYED WORK for a Tanzanian company. It is about a non-citizen working for SOMEONE ELSE. A non-citizen may hold a valid work permit to work as a chief doctor — but if they open their own private clinic, they violate GN 487A. These are two different systems.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025
next_review_trigger: Amendment to GN 487A or immigration regulations

question_sw: Je, uwekezaji wa moja kwa moja wa kigeni (FDI) unaathiriwa na GN 487A?
answer_sw: FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) na uwekezaji wa kimataifa mkubwa unaosimamiwa na TIC (Tanzania Investment Centre) na sheria ya uwekezaji unaweza kuwa na mwongozo tofauti kutoka kwa GN 487A. TIC inaweza kutoa hati za uwekezaji zinazomruhusu mgeni kufanya biashara kwa masharti maalum. Hata hivyo: FDI inayofanya biashara katika makundi yaliyopigwa marufuku na GN 487A (rejareja ndogo, salon, nk) bila idhini maalum ya TIC inaweza bado kukiuka GN 487A. Thibitisha hali yako na TIC na Idara ya Uhamiaji.
question_en: Does foreign direct investment (FDI) get affected by GN 487A?
answer_en: FDI and large international investments managed through TIC (Tanzania Investment Centre) and investment law may have different guidance from GN 487A. TIC may issue investment certificates that permit a non-citizen to conduct business under specific conditions. However: FDI conducting businesses in GN 487A prohibited categories (small retail, salons, etc.) without specific TIC authorisation may still violate GN 487A. Verify your situation with TIC and the Immigration Department.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025
next_review_trigger: Amendment to GN 487A or investment law

question_sw: Mgeni mwenye ruhusa ya ukaazi wa kudumu (permanent residence permit) — ana haki ya kufanya rejareja?
answer_sw: Hapana — ruhusa ya ukaazi wa kudumu (permanent residence) inakuruhusu kuishi Tanzania kwa muda mrefu lakini haikubadilishi hadhi yako ya 'mgeni' kwa madhumuni ya GN 487A. GN 487A inaangalia URAIA wa Tanzania — si hali ya ukaazi. Mgeni mwenye ukaazi wa kudumu bado anakabiliwa na vikwazo vya GN 487A kwa biashara. Njia pekee ya kubadilisha hadhi hii ni kupata uraia wa Tanzania rasmi.
question_en: A non-citizen with a permanent residence permit — do they have the right to conduct retail trade?
answer_en: No — a permanent residence permit allows you to live in Tanzania long-term but does not change your 'non-citizen' status for GN 487A purposes. GN 487A looks at Tanzanian CITIZENSHIP — not residency status. A non-citizen with permanent residence still faces GN 487A restrictions on business. The only way to change this status is to obtain Tanzanian citizenship formally.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025
next_review_trigger: Amendment to GN 487A or citizenship law

question_sw: GN 487A ilianza kutumika tarehe gani hasa — na operesheni ya utekelezaji ilifanyika lini?
answer_sw: GN 487A ilianza kutumika tarehe 28 Julai 2025 — siku hiyo hiyo ilitangazwa kwenye Gazeti la Serikali. Operesheni ya utekelezaji ilifanywa na Idara ya Uhamiaji katika miezi iliyofuata tarehe ya gazeti ya 28 Julai 2025. Thibitisha hali ya sasa ya utekelezaji na Idara ya Uhamiaji moja kwa moja. Jina kamili la amri: Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025. Kutaja mwaka mwingine wowote (2023 au 2024) ni kosa — amri hii ni ya 2025.
question_en: On exactly what date did GN 487A take effect — and when did the enforcement operation happen?
answer_en: GN 487A took effect on 28 July 2025 — the same day it was gazetted in the Government Gazette. An enforcement operation was conducted by the Immigration Department in the months following the gazette date of 28 July 2025. Verify current enforcement status with the Immigration Department directly. Full name of the order: Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025. Citing any other year (2023 or 2024) is an error — this order is from 2025.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025

question_sw: Mgeni anamiliki hisa 49% na Mtanzania ana 51% — biashara ya rejareja ni halali?
answer_sw: Umiliki wa hisa 51% na Mtanzania ni hatua nzuri lakini si dhamana kamili ya kuzuia tatizo la GN 487A. Idara ya Uhamiaji inachunguza: ni nani anayeendesha biashara halisi, ni nani mwenye nguvu za uamuzi, na kama umiliki wa Mtanzania ni wa kweli au wa bandia. Ikiwa mgeni ana 49% lakini ana nguvu kamili za uamuzi na Mtanzania ni mmiliki wa jina tu — hali hii inaweza kuzingatiwa ukiukaji. Muundo wa kisheria lazima uwe wa kweli.
question_en: A non-citizen owns 49% of shares and a Tanzanian owns 51% — is retail trade legal?
answer_en: A Tanzanian 51% shareholding is a good step but is not a complete guarantee against a GN 487A problem. The Immigration Department investigates: who actually runs the business, who holds decision-making power, and whether the Tanzanian ownership is genuine or nominal. If a non-citizen has 49% but holds full decision-making power and the Tanzanian is owner in name only — this situation may be treated as a violation. The legal structure must be genuine.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025
next_review_trigger: Amendment to GN 487A or related case law

question_sw: Je, kuna mgawanyo wowote kati ya GN 487A na biashara za kidijitali (online business) za wageni?
answer_sw: GN 487A inazuia biashara kwa wageni Tanzania Bara — lakini jinsi inavyotumika kwa biashara za kidijitali (online) bado si wazi kabisa katika mwongozo rasmi. Biashara ya kidijitali ambayo kimsingi inafanya 'retail trade' ya bidhaa na wateja wa Tanzania inaweza kuzingatiwa ikiwa ndani ya mipaka ya GN 487A hata kama inafanyika mtandaoni. Mwongozo huu maalum bado unaendelea kuwa katika mchakato wa kubainishwa. Thibitisha na Idara ya Uhamiaji na TRA.
question_en: Is there any distinction between GN 487A and non-citizen digital (online) businesses?
answer_en: GN 487A prohibits businesses by non-citizens in Tanzania Mainland — but how it applies to digital (online) businesses is not yet entirely clear in official guidance. An online business that in essence conducts 'retail trade' of goods with Tanzanian customers may be considered within GN 487A's scope even if conducted online. This specific guidance is still in the process of being clarified. Verify with the Immigration Department and TRA.
primary_source_name: TanzLII - GN 487A Business Licensing (Prohibition of Business Activities for Non-Citizens) Order 2025
next_review_trigger: Regulatory guidance on digital business and GN 487A

question_sw: Kwa muhtasari wa mada ngumu ya GN 487A: vitu 4 muhimu ambavyo mfanyabiashara yeyote lazima avijue.
answer_sw: Vitu 4 muhimu vya GN 487A kwa mfanyabiashara: (1) NANI: Wageni (non-citizens) tu — Watanzania hawakabiwi vikwazo vya GN 487A. (2) NINI: Makundi 15 ya biashara yakiwemo rejareja, jumla, mobile money, ukarabati wa simu, salon, kinyozi, ushonaji, na mengine. (3) ADHABU: Mgeni = angalau TZS 10M NA kifungo NA visa kufutwa; Msaidizi Mtanzania = hadi TZS 5M AU kifungo miezi 3. (4) NJIA ZA KUKWEPA HAZIFANYI KAZI: Ndoa, ukaazi wa muda mrefu, kampuni ya Tanzania, 49%/51% bandia — zote hazizuii GN 487A bila uraia wa kweli wa Tanzania.
question_en: Summary of the complex GN 487A topic: 4 critical things any business person must know.
answer_en: 4 critical GN 487A things for any business person: (1) WHO: Non-citizens only — Tanzanians are not subject to GN 487A restrictions. (2) WHAT: 15 business categories including retail, wholesale, mobile money, phone repair, hair salons, barbershops, tailoring, and others. (3) PENALTIES: Non-citizen = at least TZS 10M AND imprisonment AND visa revocation; Tanzanian facilitator = up to TZS 5M OR 3 months' imprisonment.
